mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% over three months signals a tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST declines for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by >1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during three consecutive months of >1% INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% and 4% respectively, sustained for two months, signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment that erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 4% for 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive monetary policy regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL > 4% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three months, coupled with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces demand for equities and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo MA by >10% for 3 months AND GDPC1 flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) under the specified RSAFS and GDPC1 conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 400k per month for three consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when PAYEMS exceeds 400,000 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which raises earnings expectations and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during four consecutive months of >0.5% INDPRO increases.
